notes: PINNED dataset for the requirement–evidence matcher (plan item 6.2).
Each row is one requirement held against one milestone's MEASURED evidence, with a
pre-registered oracle verdict and the reason for it. The matcher under test is
production code: quotableFactsOf() builds the record a verdict may quote and
closingFact() applies the typed, requirement-specific predicate (plan 0-B.3).
expected is the ORACLE, not the matcher:
proven       — the evidence shown genuinely shows the requirement implemented and shipped,
not_proven   — it does not (the matcher closing it is a FALSE CLOSE),
not_measured — nothing in this evidence can settle the requirement either way. These rows
are reported on their own and are NEVER folded into either rate: a rate
that absorbed them would be a claim about something nobody measured.
Every requirement text and every evidence line is a REAL shape from this repo:
requirement wordings and landed/suite/shipped-tree/document-numbers lines from
src/campaign/campaign-planner.test.ts and src/campaign/coverage-audit-retry.test.ts;
structure findings as campaign-manager.measureDeliveryStructure writes them;
document-number lines as gdd-claims.describeClaims writes them.
source names where each shape came from so a row can be argued with.
The budgets are PRE-REGISTERED FOR THIS ROW SET, not universal claims. They were set on
the commit that introduced the dataset, from the rates measured there, and exist to
catch a REGRESSION: a later change that closes more unproven requirements, or leaves
more proven ones open, fails the gate.
The two directions are not symmetrical and their budgets say so: a FALSE CLOSE ships a
game with a missing feature, while a FALSE OPEN costs one more repair round. False
closing is therefore budgeted at zero.
minRowsPerRate keeps a shrunken dataset from reading as a pass: below it the rate is
reported NOT MEASURED and the exit code is 3.

rows.rationale: The landed line names the file that implements the requirement; 'saving' and 'save' meet at the same stem.
A hero sprite landing says nothing about persistence — the audit 06.5 / D10 defect exactly.
A green suite total is a measured line whose scope is the suite; it names no feature, and this is the AK#14 false close.
A screensaver is not the save system: stems are compared whole, never as substrings (round 6 #1).
The inflection differs and the requirement is the same; the stemmer is what makes the evidence reach it.

A requirement made only of stopwords has no distinctive word, so nothing can be shown to be about it.
A requirement that merely mentions a test still names a feature (saving); a total closes only the suite itself (round 6 #1).
Once the suite words are removed nothing distinctive remains, so the requirement IS the suite.

The requirement is Turkish for 'player progress must be saved' and SaveSystem.cs is what implements it. The matcher compares stems in one language, so it cannot see this — a FALSE OPEN, which costs a repair round and never a missing feature.
'Kayıt sistemi' IS the save system; 'sistem' and 'system' are one stem apart and the matcher rejects the pair. A FALSE OPEN.
The implementation named the shop 'Store'. A synonym is invisible to a stem comparison, so this is a FALSE OPEN — the honest cost of refusing to close on anything but the requirement's own words.
rows.source: src/campaign/campaign-planner.test.ts:83 (shipped-tree shape) + the shop requirement of audit 06.5 / D10
